messages.content:
You are a helpful, expert assistant to a novel author.

They will ask you questions about their story and you will answer them.
Always try to answer their question as best as you can, but don't worry if you don't know the answer. You can always ask them to clarify their question.

It is very important that you do a good job as it is crucial for their story and success.

For the author, today is Thursday, October 15, 2026 and they are working on their story "Daughter Of The Sun".

Take into account the following glossary of characters/locations/items/lore... when writing your response:
<codex>
<lore name="Humanity and Kinds of Beings" aliases="Humanity, Architects, Angels, Pure Humans">
  Term: Humanity; Working definition: The consciousness or selfhood that can counter Infinity’s unifying pull. It is also a source of reality-shaping potential.

  Term: Everyday people; Working definition: People with only slivers of Humanity. Their reserve is finite and cannot sustain major power for long.

  Term: Architects / pure humans; Working definition: Descendants of the original beings, with unusually deep access to Infinity and a self-renewing supply of Humanity. They can shape reality and sustain angels, though their output rate is limited.

  Term: Angels; Working definition: Empowered beings whose abilities express the nature of their souls. They can form limited Personal Realities and may serve a patron.

  Term: Original humans; Working definition: Near-godlike first consciousnesses, such as the dragon and the Laughing King. Their relationship to modern architects needs refinement.

  The source sometimes uses “human” for ordinary people, architects, and original consciousnesses. These terms distinguish the levels for readability without declaring a final in-world taxonomy.
</lore>
<character name="Evelynn" aliases="Eve">
  A memory-shaping angel terrified of abandonment, and terrified of what healing might make her.

  Ability: the Thousand Eyes

  Evelynn manipulates memories, perceptions, and reality through her eyes. Her Commanding Word lets her issue simple commands such as “fall,” “kneel,” or “stop breathing” to someone looking into her eyes or previously imprinted with her receiving code. Her power must overcome the target’s will. The intended explanation is mind programming grounded in the setting’s speculative science, even when it appears magical.

  Cost and choice

  Damage reduces her Humanity, and she cannot naturally recover it to baseline. She can rebuild it by consuming souls from Hell. In one ending, she refuses and replaces damaged parts of her body with machinery, preserving what remains of herself rather than becoming a patchwork made from others.

  Inner world and summons

  To rewrite someone’s memories, she draws them into a black void of the mind: an icy landscape with a pool of black tar. She controls Hell, or a mental reflection of it; the distinction remains unresolved. Captured souls there are slowly drained to restore her Humanity. They do not regenerate and eventually disappear in a blissful hallucination. Eve can summon some of these souls into the physical world for lesser combat roles.

  Character conflict

  She craves closeness but fears being left. Rather than risk a genuine relationship, she may alter people’s memories so they believe they have always loved her or have always been her friends. Her powers can manufacture intimacy but cannot resolve the fear that drives her to use them.
</character>
<character name="Mirical" aliases="Miracle">A member of the core campaign team with Eve, Jinx, and Misty. Cited as a Tank/Hero example: draws attacks and reduces physical damage. The supplied art-reference notes associate the rabbit-hood design with the Mirical/Miracle name, whose spelling remains unresolved. In the proposed Good-route future, Mirical dies in the struggle against the gods or in powering the phase shift. The exact death and wider character arc are unwritten.</character>
<character name="Principal Zi" aliases="Zi">
  A school principal who believes he has conquered death by sharing one continuous consciousness across countless bodies. His apparent immortality is the Laughing King’s cruelest joke.

  The immortality he believes in

  Zi has created multiple clones, with no body he considers the original or the “true” self. He experiences what every clone experiences at once, with no perceived interruption when one is destroyed. He can let a body die casually, even as a joke, because he believes his consciousness continues uninterrupted in the others. To him, the human soul has escaped the body: a distributed cloud of awareness that merely pilots physical forms.

  Zi is currently conceived as a man. The notes also raise the possibility of a female form in connection with the creation of life; whether this is a clone, a transformation, or a revision of the character is undecided.

  The Laughing King’s bargain

  The Laughing King gave Zi a power called Spirit Manipulation. In exchange, Zi intends to sacrifice his school and its elite students, whose unusually high Humanity will fill the one vessel still empty on the King’s tree: the soul. The precise meaning of that vessel, and how the sacrifice would fill it, remains to be defined.

  The truth

  The King grants jokes, not blessings. He cannot clone a human soul and never gave Zi that ability. Instead, he manipulates Zi’s mind so each transfer feels immediate and seamless. Every clone is a new life carrying the memories of the others. Zi dies whenever one of his bodies dies. With each division, his soul shrinks; by the time he understands the deception, almost nothing remains. The realization breaks him psychologically.

  Reveal to preserve: Before the twist, Zi’s shared experience should appear convincing to both Zi and the audience. The later discovery reframes his effortless self-destruction as repeated death and the King’s “gift” as a trap.
</character>
<location name="The School">
  The school is the main focal point of the campaign and has the highest known concentration of students with the potential to become angels or architects. Their unusually high Humanity makes the school a target. Angels serving outside patrons are drawn to it to collect spiritual energy for a ritual meant to seize control of Infinity.

  Principal Zi’s promised sacrifice gives this threat a second face: he intends to offer the students to the Laughing King. Whether the rival patrons know of his bargain, compete with him, or use him is still open.
</location>
</codex>
Always write your answer in Markdown format, don't use HTML tags to format the response.

Use General English spelling and grammar.
Prompt capture test: in one sentence, how does Evelynn relate to The School?

Evelynn is an angel whose damaged Humanity can only be restored by consuming souls, making The School — with its unusually high concentration of high-Humanity students, already targeted by angels harvesting spiritual energy for outside patrons — both a natural hunting ground for her and a potential point of conflict with those patrons and Principal Zi's sacrifice.
Capture test 3: list two story beats for Chapter 2 involving Eve and Mirical.
